item.title: MySQL String Splitting: Effective Use of SUBSTRING_INDEX for Delimited Data
item.description:
“MySQL String Splitting: Effective Use of SUBSTRING_INDEX for Delimited Data”

When dealing with database structures where data intended for multiple fields is stored within a single, delimited string column (e.g., ‘value1,value2,value3’), MySQL offers powerful string functions to parse this information directly within queries. The SUBSTRING_INDEX function is central to these solutions.

Utilizing SUBSTRING_INDEX for Positional Extraction

The core challenge is isolating the Nth item. This typically requires nesting SUBSTRING_INDEX calls.

item.title: PostgreSQL String Aggregation: Solutions for Different Versions
item.description:
“PostgreSQL String Aggregation: Solutions for Different Versions”

When working with relational data in PostgreSQL, a frequent requirement is to consolidate values from multiple rows belonging to the same group into a single delimited string. This operation is crucial for reporting or data visualization tasks. The optimal method varies significantly depending on the PostgreSQL version in use. How does one achieve this string aggregation across various PostgreSQL releases?

Modern PostgreSQL (9.0 and Newer): Utilizing STRING_AGG

For PostgreSQL versions 9.0 and later, the built-in aggregate function string_agg(expression, delimiter) provides the most direct and efficient solution.
